name: AD7745ARUZ-REEL7
title: AD7745/AD7746: 24-bit capacitance-to-digital converters with temperature sensor
summary: A sigma-delta converter that measures a floating capacitor directly: the sensor sits between an excitation pin and a capacitive input, and the result comes out over I2C as a 24-bit code covering ±4.096 pF, with up to 17 pF of fixed capacitance cancelled by on-chip CAPDACs. The same core converts a differential voltage, the supply and an internal or external temperature sensor. AD7745 has one capacitive input and AD7746 two. It runs from 2.7 V to 5.25 V at about 0.7 mA over –40°C to +125°C in a 16-lead TSSOP; AD7745ARUZ-REEL7 is the one-channel part.
key_figures: 24 bits no missing codes; 19 bits effective typ at 62 ms
±4 fF max (25°C, VDD = 5 V, after offset calibration)
2.7 V to 3.6 V or 4.75 V to 5.25 V, 850 µA max, 0.5 µA power-down

notes: Z marks a Pb-free part.

circuits.title: Basic application with a differential capacitive sensor
circuits.description: A floating differential sensor, two variable capacitors sharing a common plate, is measured with no other analog parts: the common plate is driven from EXCA, and the two free plates go to CIN1(+) and CIN1(-). VDD comes from a 3 V or 5 V rail with a 0.1 µF ceramic and a 10 µF polarised capacitor to ground. SDA and SCL each have a 10 kΩ pull-up to the rail and run to the host, which may also watch RDY. EXCB, the voltage input and the reference input are not used.

parts.note: variable, positive half of the differential sensor
variable, negative half of the differential sensor

circuits.title: Transistor as an external temperature sensor
circuits.description: A 2N3906 PNP transistor senses temperature away from the chip. Its emitter reaches VIN(+) through the wiring resistance RS1; its base and collector go to ground, and VIN(-) reaches that ground through the wiring resistance RS2. The chip sources two currents in turn into VIN(+) and converts the difference in base-emitter voltage; up to 100 Ω of total wiring resistance is compensated.
notes: Select VTMD1 = 0, VTMD0 = 1 (external temperature sensor diode).

circuits.title: Resistive temperature sensor on the voltage input
circuits.description: An RTD and a reference resistor RREF in series form one string from VDD to ground. The voltage input reads across the RTD and the reference input across RREF. The voltage and reference inputs are sampled continuously during a conversion, so the source impedance driving them is kept low.
notes: Select VTMD1 = 1, VTMD0 = 1 (external voltage input) and EXTREF = 1.

operation.text: AD7745 has one capacitive input (CIN1); AD7746 has two (CIN1, CIN2), multiplexed into one converter. Each input works single-ended or differentially. Everything else is the same on both. Both are meant for floating sensors, with neither plate grounded; The AD7747 is the part for sensors with one plate grounded.

One converter core, a second-order sigma-delta (charge-balancing) modulator followed by a third-order digital filter, serves as a capacitance-to-digital converter for the CIN inputs and as an ordinary ADC for the voltage input, the VDD monitor and the temperature sensors. Around it sit the input multiplexer, the excitation source, two CAPDACs, a temperature sensor, a voltage reference, a clock generator, control and calibration logic, and the I2C interface; no external parts are needed for capacitive sensing.

The unknown capacitance CX sits between an EXC pin and a CIN pin. During a conversion a square wave from EXC drives CX and the modulator samples the charge that passes through it. The filtered bit stream is scaled with the calibration coefficients and read over I2C. Both plates of CX must be isolated from ground.

EXCA and EXCB are programmed independently and behave alike, so either can drive the sensor, normal or inverted. On the AD7746 each capacitive channel is best given its own EXC pin. The excitation runs at 32 kHz with an amplitude of ±VDD/8, ±VDD/4, ±VDD × 3/8 or ±VDD/2 chosen by EXCLVL. EXCERR flags an excitation pin that cannot be driven, such as one shorted or loaded with too much capacitance to ground.

The full scale is ±4.096 pF (worked figures use ±4 pF). Two 7-bit CAPDACs, one on CIN(+) and one on CIN(−), subtract a fixed capacitance of up to about 17 pF to 21 pF so that a sensor with a large unchanging part can still use the ±4 pF span; they are monotonic and well matched with a defined temperature coefficient, but their full range is not factory calibrated and can be up to ±20% off. On the AD7746 the two channels share the CAPDACs; to give each channel its own setting the host reloads them before converting on the other channel.

With CAPDIFF = 0, CIN(−) is disconnected inside the chip. Without CAPDACs the input reads only positive capacitance from 0 pF to 4 pF, codes 0x800000 to 0xFFFFFF. With CAPDAC(+) at 4 pF the whole code range covers 0 pF to 8 pF; with CAPDAC(+) at 17 pF it covers 13 pF to 21 pF.

With CAPDIFF = 1 the converter reads the difference between the CIN(+) and CIN(−) capacitances, CX and CY. Each must be under 4 pF without CAPDACs, or under 21 pF with CAPDACs trimming CX − CAPDAC(+) and CY − CAPDAC(−) each below 4 pF; for example CX and CY at 17 ± 2 pF with both CAPDACs at 17 pF, or CX at 17 ± 4 pF against a fixed 17 pF CY. An unbalanced capacitance above 4 pF from EXC to CIN causes gain, offset and nonlinearity error.

Capacitance from CIN or EXC to ground ideally does not enter the result, but it slowly degrades it: up to 60 pF on CIN and 100 pF on EXC are allowed. Leakage from CX to ground adds gain, offset and nonlinearity error, with limits that tighten at lower supply. Resistance across CX passes charge and reads as extra capacitance. Total series resistance in the sensor connections should stay under 1 kΩ for specified performance.

Capacitive data: 0x000000 is −4.096 pF, 0x800000 zero, 0xFFFFFF +4.096 pF. Voltage data: 0x000000 is −VREF, 0x800000 is 0 V, 0xFFFFFF is +VREF. Temperature data converts with the temperature equation.

A data register is updated when its channel finishes a conversion, except while a bus read of that register is in progress, in which case the new result is dropped; the read ends at the stop condition. Read all three bytes of a result (six when both channels are enabled) in one auto-incrementing multibyte read, since single-byte reads can mix bytes of two results, and read each result before the next one on that channel completes.

Each part's capacitive gain is trimmed at the factory for ±4.096 pF and the coefficient is kept in one-time-programmable memory, loaded into the gain register at power-up and reset. A capacitance gain calibration with a full-scale capacitor on the input, or a write to the gain register, changes it only until the next power-up or reset. The part is specified only with the factory coefficient.

Capacitive offset is not trimmed at the factory, because in use it is set by the sensor's own starting capacitance, board traces and wiring. Offset beyond ±1 pF is taken out first with the CAPDACs; what remains within ±1 pF goes into the offset calibration register, either by connecting a zero-scale capacitance and running the offset calibration mode, which makes that input read 0x800000, or by writing a computed value (LSB 31.25 aF). The register returns to its default at power-up and reset, so the host either recalibrates or stores and reloads the value. On the AD7746 both channels share the register; to calibrate them separately the host reads the value after each channel's calibration and writes it back before converting on that channel.

An on-chip transistor is run at two currents in ratio N and the difference in its base-emitter voltage, which is linear in temperature, is converted and scaled with factory coefficients so the code is proportional to die temperature. Self-heating is under 0.5°C at VDD = 5 V. If the sensor is at the chip's temperature, the internal sensor can serve for drift compensation of the whole system. It must be used with the internal reference.

The same two-current method works with an external transistor between VIN(+) and VIN(−), modified to cancel up to 100 Ω of total wiring resistance. VIN(−) must be grounded. Calibration is for a 2N3906 with ideality factor 1.008.

The core also works as a differential-input ADC with up to 21 effective bits, using either the on-chip 1.17 V reference or an external reference on the differential REFIN pins. Both the voltage and reference inputs are sampled continuously during a conversion, so they should be driven from a low impedance.
With VTMD = 10 the ADC converts VDD, divided inside the chip by 6.

The capacitive channel runs from 11.0 ms (90.9 Hz) to 109.6 ms (9.1 Hz) per conversion, and the voltage/temperature channel from 20.1 ms to 122.1 ms, both chosen in the configuration register. Longer conversions give lower noise. At 62 ms the capacitive channel rejects 50 Hz by 65 dB and 60 Hz by 55 dB together. CLKCTRL = 1 doubles every conversion time.

MD2 to MD0 pick the mode: the converter can sit idle, convert once or repeatedly, power down, or run a system calibration (capacitive offset; capacitive or voltage gain). Each channel joins conversions only when its enable bit (CAPEN, VTEN) is set.

The part is an I2C slave at start byte 0x90 for write and 0x91 for read, SCL up to 400 kHz. A write carries the register address pointer first and then data bytes to successive registers. A read returns data from the current pointer, incrementing while the master acknowledges. A stop resets the pointer to 0x00 (the status register), so the status can be polled by repeated reads without rewriting the pointer. Past the last register, reads return internal contents until the master ends the transfer, and writes are acknowledged but discarded.

Writing 0xBF as the address pointer resets the part and reloads all defaults without resetting the bus. A general call (address 0x00) followed by 0x06 does the same; other general call commands are not acknowledged. During the reload, about 150 µs and at most 200 µs, the part does not acknowledge.

Decouple VDD to GND with a low-impedance capacitor, for example 10 µF tantalum in parallel with 0.1 µF multilayer ceramic. SCL and SDA need pull-ups if the bus has none. Unused RDY and EXC pins are left open; unused CIN, VIN and REFIN pins may be left open or grounded; NC pins are left open.
